intent.direction: The backdrop fades while the card pops a beat behind it. The card is the focal point, so it takes the emphasis role and a `quick` delay.
Card and backdrop leave together, fast.
The backdrop fades while the panel crosses into place from its edge.
The panel leaves the way it came; the backdrop follows, shorter.
The backdrop fades while the panel crosses into place from its edge.
The panel leaves the way it came; the backdrop follows, shorter.
The thumb squashes as it leaves and stretches as it lands.
Rows rise into place one after another, capped so a long list is not slow.
Rows sink away from the last one up, faster than they arrived.
Each line rises out of its own mask. Storytelling only; never on product UI.
Height eases open; never a jump cut.
Height eases closed, faster than it opened.
A floating layer grows out of its trigger: a short pop on the disclosure role.
Gets out of the way, faster than it came.
The toast springs in: pop, overshoot, settle.

transform: translateX(calc(var(--switch-from) + (var(--switch-to) - var(--switch-from)) * 0.9)) scaleX(calc(1 + var(--motion-squash))) scaleY(calc(1 - var(--motion-squash)))

instant.direction: No animation: the change happens at once.

fade.direction: The cross-fade that replaces travel and scale when motion is reduced.

quick.direction: The fastest perceptible response; reads near-instant.

short.direction: Small content entering; fast but visible.

medium.direction: Functional motion that needs a little more time.

extra-long.direction: Expressive, still part of using the product.

super-long.direction: Meant to be noticed rather than used.

cinematic.direction: Storytelling only; never on a control.

use-hover.direction: Fast and responsive; the most frequent interaction on desktop.

use-focus.direction: Same speed as hover; the entrance curve lets the ring settle as someone tabs through.

use-press.direction: Immediate; the exit curve reads as a press going down.

use-disclosure-in.direction: Small content appearing next to its trigger; time to settle.

use-disclosure-out.direction: Gets out of the way quickly.

use-overlay-in.direction: The layer that covers the page arriving.

use-overlay-out.direction: An overlay leaving; shorter than its entrance.

use-emphasis-in.direction: The element the eye should land on; the expressive curve, a beat behind its backdrop.

use-travel-in.direction: A panel crossing the screen into place.

use-travel-out.direction: The panel leaving the way it came.

use-toggle.direction: A state change the thumb travels across.

use-stagger-in.direction: One child of a staggered reveal.

use-stagger-out.direction: One child of a staggered dismissal.

use-reveal.direction: Storytelling: slow, deliberate, meant to be watched.

use-celebration.direction: Expressive and long; rare by design.

use-color.direction: Slow and symmetric so a colour shift does not flash.

use-loop.direction: Continuous motion: linear, one full turn per cycle.

usage: any functional entrance with no role of its own
any functional exit with no role of its own

base-functional-standard.direction: Fallback for UI that changes without entering or leaving.

Color Semantics.content/secondary: Secondary text — labels, section headings, captions, metadata. The lower of the two accessible text levels.
Color Semantics.content/tertiary: NON-ESSENTIAL only — placeholder text, input hints, watermarks. Not captions or metadata: in dark mode this step sits at Lc 27 and cannot be read. Use content-secondary for anything a reader must read.
Color Semantics.content/quaternary: NON-ESSENTIAL only — decorative marks, disabled hints. Never carries information.
Color Semantics.content/inverse: Ink on solid fills — brand buttons, status solids. White in both themes: the solid tone is SOLVED to carry it (see recToneFor).
Color Semantics.background/primary-hover: Hover state for the primary background.
Color Semantics.background/secondary-hover: Hover state for the secondary surface.
Color Semantics.border/brand-alt: Brand border; turns gray in dark mode.
Color Semantics.Surface/page: [ROLE: Base Background] Elevation level 0. Root application background. content.primary and content.secondary must maintain WCAG AA (4.5:1) against this token.
Color Semantics.Surface/layer-1: [ROLE: Container Background] Elevation level 1. Cards, panels, grouped content. Must read slightly distinct from surface.page.
Color Semantics.Surface/layer-2: [ROLE: Elevated Background] Elevation level 2. Popovers, dropdowns, modals. Pair with box-shadow in CSS — the color step alone does not convey floating.
Color Semantics.Surface/input: [ROLE: Form Background] Background for interactive data-entry fields. Ensures content.primary typed by the user stays legible. Same tone as surface.page by design — named separately so forms have their own token.
Color Semantics.Surface/selected: [ROLE: Active State Background] Subtle fill for mutual selection (e.g. a selected table row). Must guarantee 4.5:1 against content.primary on top.
Color Semantics.Surface/selected-pressed: [ROLE: Active State Background Pressed] A pressed soft brand control (Button Soft / Outline pressed). {accent-a.5}, two steps deeper than surface.selected — the brand twin of status.*.surface-pressed.
Color Semantics.Surface/inverse: [ROLE: Inverted Background] High-contrast background for tooltips and snackbars. Always pair with content.inverse. Light {neutral.12}; dark {neutral-dark.11} — a muted inverse chip, not the dark ramp's near-white step.
Color Semantics.Surface/overlay: [ROLE: Scrim] Semi-transparent layer over surface.page to focus attention on modals (layer-2 surfaces). Ships at 60% black alpha (`{black-a.8}`), same in both themes.
Color Semantics.Surface/accent: [ROLE: Accent Wash] Ambient brand-tinted background — a section that leans brand without being an interactive fill.
Color Semantics.Surface/muted: [ROLE: Control Track] Neutral fill of a control's passive part — a Switch's off track, a Slider or Progress track, an OTP segment, a step connector. {neutral.4} in light. Not a button: a secondary CTA uses action.secondary.default.
Color Semantics.Surface/muted-hover: [ROLE: Control Track Hover] Hover twin of surface.muted (a hovered off Switch, a scrollbar thumb). {neutral.5} in light — one step past the track.
Color Semantics.Content/primary: [ROLE: High Contrast Text] Main body and headings. STRICT: must pass WCAG AA (4.5:1) against surface.page and surface.layer-1.
Color Semantics.Content/secondary: [ROLE: Medium Contrast Text] Supporting copy and descriptions. STRICT: WCAG AA (4.5:1) against standard surface backgrounds.
Color Semantics.Content/subtle: [ROLE: Low Contrast Text] Placeholders and decorative de-emphasis only — not a third readable body tier. Minimum ~3:1; do not convey information.
Color Semantics.Content/disabled: [ROLE: Inactive Text] Disabled controls and copy. Exempt from strict WCAG rules — must communicate inactivity, not full legibility.
Color Semantics.Content/inverse: [ROLE: Inverted Text] Required when the background is surface.inverse or any dark/solid fill outside the accent.
Color Semantics.Content/on-action: [ROLE: Button Text] Label ink used ONLY on action.primary.default. Solved per theme against that fill — never assume white. Must exceed 4.5:1 against the button fill.
Color Semantics.Content/on-secondary: [ROLE: Secondary Button Text] Label ink used ONLY on action.secondary.*. {neutral.12} in light — content.primary while secondary is a light wash; re-pointed with the fill when a system makes secondary a dark button. Must exceed 4.5:1 against the fill.
Color Semantics.Content/accent: [ROLE: Accent Text] Brand-tinted emphasis — active nav, non-link accent copy. Low-contrast text step (~4.5:1 AA against the page).
Color Semantics.Content/link/default: [ROLE: Interactive Text Default] Actionable link text. Must contrast with the background (4.5:1) and remain distinguishable from adjacent content.primary (~3:1). Uses the ramp text step, not a fill-hover step.
Color Semantics.Content/link/hover: [ROLE: Interactive Text Hover] Hover/focus variation of content.link.default — one ramp step for visible feedback while staying accessible.
Color Semantics.Action/primary/default: [ROLE: Primary CTA Default] Primary call-to-action fill. Inner text must always be content.on-action. Solved per theme — not pinned to a fixed accent step.
Color Semantics.Action/primary/hover: [ROLE: Primary CTA Hover] Affects the hover state of the primary button fill. SOLVED ({step:accent+1}) — one tone past whatever action.primary.default RESOLVED to, re-verified for label contrast, never a fixed step. (History: a pinned {accent.10} measured as low as 1.78:1 WCAG for any hue whose solid resolves above tone 9.)
Color Semantics.Action/primary/pressed: [ROLE: Primary CTA Pressed] Affects the pressed / active state of the primary button fill. SOLVED ({step:accent+2}) — two tones past the resolved default, same reasoning as hover. (History: a fixed dark {accent.6} measured APCA Lc 0-24, illegible, once the solid resolves above tone 9.)
Color Semantics.Action/secondary/default: [ROLE: Secondary CTA Default] Affects the resting fill of neutral / secondary buttons. {neutral.4} — one step heavier than surface.layer-2 so a control reads with more presence than a passive surface. Label text must be content.on-secondary, not content.on-action. Buttons and badges only — a track reads surface.muted.
Color Semantics.Action/secondary/hover: [ROLE: Secondary CTA Hover] Affects the hover state of the neutral / secondary button fill. {neutral.5} — one step past action.secondary.default, the same default → hover → pressed shape action.primary follows. Label stays content.on-secondary.
Color Semantics.Action/secondary/pressed: [ROLE: Secondary CTA Pressed] Affects the pressed / active state of the neutral / secondary button fill. {neutral.5} in light (tone 6 fails the Lc 60 label floor there), {neutral-dark.6} in dark — so light pressed shares the hover tone. Label stays content.on-secondary.
Color Semantics.Action/disabled/default: [ROLE: Disabled Default]  Affects the fill of disabled buttons and controls. An ALPHA wash — {black-a.3} in light, {white-a.2} in dark — so it reads as "muted" over the page or over a card alike, and never collides with an opaque surface. No contrast floor: it communicates inactivity, not legibility.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/default: [ROLE: Ghost Default] Resting fill of a borderless button — fully transparent (`{neutral-a.1}` — alpha-ladder step 1 is 0%, an existing primitive, so it still aliases in Figma), so the ghost tier reads default / hover / pressed like primary and secondary.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/hover: [ROLE: Ghost Hover] Hover wash for a borderless button with no brand intent (toolbar icons, close buttons, menu items). Flips ink per appearance — {black-a.1} in light, {white-a.1} in dark — because a neutral wash has to darken a light page and lighten a dark one.
Color Semantics.Action/ghost/pressed: [ROLE: Ghost Pressed] Pressed wash for a neutral borderless button. One step deeper than the hover, same black/white flip.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Affects error alerts, banners, toasts, destructive row-menu items. Tinted background. Pair with status.critical.content — never a fixed ink on the bg alone.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/surface-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Pressed] Affects a pressed destructive borderless action (a held-down Delete in a row menu), a "dismiss" on an error banner. {error-a.5} — two steps deeper than status.critical.surface. Absorbed from the old action.ghost.danger.pressed.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/surface-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Pressed] Affects a pressed warning-tinted interactive surface. {warning-a.5}.
Color Semantics.Status/success/surface-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Pressed] Affects a pressed success-tinted interactive surface. {success-a.5}.
Color Semantics.Status/info/surface-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Pressed] Affects a pressed info-tinted interactive surface. {info-a.5}.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Affects destructive badges, pills and buttons. Solid fill. Pair with status.critical.on-solid. {error.solid} in BOTH themes — solved per appearance so it lands near the anchor; the old dark {error.12} rendered a pale pink #ffddd5 because tone 12 is the near-white end of a dark ramp.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Affects the text and glyph inside an error alert, banner or toast. Ink on status.critical.surface. {error.11} in both themes — Radix's chromatic-text step, NOT tone 12 (which reads near-black on a pale tint and near-white on a dark one, losing the severity hue).
Color Semantics.Status/critical/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.critical.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/surface-solid-hover: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Hover] Hover of status.critical.surface-solid (a critical button). SOLVED ({step:error+1}) — one tone past the resolved solid that still carries status.critical.on-solid.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/surface-solid-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Pressed] Pressed of status.critical.surface-solid. SOLVED ({step:error+2}).
Color Semantics.Status/warning/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Tinted background for warning alerts. Pair with status.warning.content.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Affects the text and glyph inside a warning alert, banner or toast. Ink on status.warning.surface. {warning.11} in both themes — the chromatic-text step, not tone 12. Often byte-identical to warning.border-strong and warning.surface-solid: the warning ramp has one tone that is both chromatic text, the 3:1 boundary and the solved solid. Three roles, one step — keep all three names.
Color Semantics.Status/success/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Tinted background for success alerts. Pair with status.success.content.
Color Semantics.Status/success/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Affects the text and glyph inside a success alert, banner or toast. Ink on status.success.surface. {success.11} in both themes — the chromatic-text step, not tone 12.
Color Semantics.Status/info/surface: [ROLE: Feedback Background Subtle] Tinted background for informational alerts and banners. Pair with status.info.content — never a fixed ink on the bg alone.
Color Semantics.Status/info/content: [ROLE: Feedback Text] Affects the text and glyph inside an informational alert, banner or toast. Ink on status.info.surface. {info.11} in both themes — the chromatic-text step, not tone 12.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Affects warning badges, pills and buttons. Solid fill. Pair with status.warning.on-solid. {warning.solid} in both themes — solved per appearance. On this ramp the solid lands on tone 11, the same step as content and border-strong. Do not delete the role because of that collision.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.warning.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill, never assumed white — a warning solid is usually light enough to need dark ink.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/surface-solid-hover: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Hover] Hover of status.warning.surface-solid (a warning button). SOLVED ({step:warning+1}) — one tone past the resolved solid that still carries status.warning.on-solid.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/surface-solid-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Pressed] Pressed of status.warning.surface-solid. SOLVED ({step:warning+2}).
Color Semantics.Status/success/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Affects success badges, pills and buttons. Solid fill. Pair with status.success.on-solid. {success.solid} in both themes — solved per appearance.
Color Semantics.Status/success/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.success.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill.
Color Semantics.Status/success/surface-solid-hover: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Hover] Hover of status.success.surface-solid (a success button). SOLVED ({step:success+1}) — one tone past the resolved solid that still carries status.success.on-solid.
Color Semantics.Status/success/surface-solid-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Pressed] Pressed of status.success.surface-solid. SOLVED ({step:success+2}).
Color Semantics.Status/info/surface-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid] Affects info badges, pills and buttons. Solid fill. Pair with status.info.on-solid. {info.solid} in both themes — solved per appearance.
Color Semantics.Status/info/on-solid: [ROLE: Feedback Inverted Text] Label ink on status.info.surface-solid. Solved per theme against that fill.
Color Semantics.Status/info/surface-solid-hover: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Hover] Hover of status.info.surface-solid (a info button). SOLVED ({step:info+1}) — one tone past the resolved solid that still carries status.info.on-solid.
Color Semantics.Status/info/surface-solid-pressed: [ROLE: Feedback Background Solid Pressed] Pressed of status.info.surface-solid. SOLVED ({step:info+2}).
Color Semantics.Status/critical/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] Affects alerts, banners, toasts. The stroke around a critical message — the edge of a MESSAGE, not a control boundary, so it is not measured for WCAG 1.4.11 (the severity is carried by status.critical.content and the glyph). An alpha primitive, {error-a.6}, because the tint it sits on is alpha too: a solid stroke over a translucent fill composites against a different backdrop than the fill and the two drift apart on any non-page surface. For a stroke that DOES bear a boundary obligation — an invalid input — use status.critical.border-strong.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] Affects alerts, banners, toasts. The stroke around a warning message. {warning-a.6}. See status.critical.border for why it is alpha and why it carries no contrast floor.
Color Semantics.Status/success/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] Affects alerts, banners, toasts. The stroke around a success message. {success-a.6}. See status.critical.border.
Color Semantics.Status/info/border: [ROLE: Feedback Border] Affects alerts, banners, toasts. The stroke around an informational message. {info-a.6}. See status.critical.border.
Color Semantics.Status/critical/border-strong: [ROLE: Critical Control Boundary] Affects invalid form fields, error-state inputs and selects. The stroke IS the control, so WCAG 1.4.11 + APCA Lc 45 apply — unlike status.critical.border (the edge of a banner). Light {error.9} = 3.76:1/Lc64. Dark {error.11} = 11.94:1 — error.9/10 fail APCA in dark (Lc 37.6/44.2), the border.control blind spot.
Color Semantics.Status/warning/border-strong: [ROLE: Warning Control Boundary] Affects form fields in a warning state. {warning.11} — the minimum tone clearing WCAG in light (tone 9 = 2.35, tone 10 = 2.74, both fail). Same step as warning.content / warning.surface-solid on every seed measured; the jobs stay distinct even when the hex does not.
Color Semantics.Status/success/border-strong: [ROLE: Success Control Boundary] Affects validated / success-state form fields. {success.10} — one step lighter than warning/critical; this ramp clears both metrics a full step earlier (3.32:1/Lc60 light, 8.21:1/Lc56 dark).
Color Semantics.Status/info/border-strong: [ROLE: Info Control Boundary] Affects informational-state form fields. Light {info.9} = 3.24:1/Lc59. Dark {info.10} = 7.15:1/Lc49 — info.9 fails APCA in dark (Lc 42), one step earlier than error needs.
Color Semantics.Border/subtle: [ROLE: Decorative Border 1/3] Affects hairline dividers, table rules, the edge of a quiet grouping. Lightest neutral stroke — {black-a.2} in light, {white-a.2} in dark (the FIXED alpha ladder, so it composites correctly on any surface). One step above the 5% rung: that step measured APCA Lc 0 on the dark page. DECORATION: separates regions, carries no state, no contrast floor. If the stroke is the only thing telling the user a control is there, that is border.control.
Color Semantics.Border/default: [ROLE: Decorative Border 2/3] Affects a card edge, a panel boundary, a grouping box. {black-a.3} / {white-a.3}. DECORATION, no contrast floor. One step above border.subtle so a panel edge still outranks a hairline.
Color Semantics.Border/control: [ROLE: Control Boundary] Affects the resting border of inputs, textareas, selects, checkboxes, radios, switch tracks and outline buttons. A HAIRLINE at the weight modern systems draw it (shadcn's --border): SOLVED on the alpha ladder ({ctl-a:…}) to a 1.4:1 visibility floor, the first step visibly off the page — {black-a.3} (1.41:1) in light, {white-a.3} (1.50:1) in dark for the default system. It does NOT clear WCAG 1.4.11 on its own by design: a control that must be identified without a fill gives itself one (surface.input a step off the page).
Color Semantics.Border/control-hover: [ROLE: Control Boundary Hover] Affects the hover state of a control's resting (border.control) border. One step past whatever border.control RESOLVED to ({ctl+a:…}), never a fixed step — pinning it would collapse it onto rest. {black-a.4} / {white-a.4} for the default system. The Figma plugin draws every control's hover stroke from this concept.
Color Semantics.Border/strong: [ROLE: Strong Border] Affects the edge of a grouping or a selected container that must read before its neighbours. Not the field outline — that is border.control. WCAG 1.4.11 + APCA Lc 45 against the page, SOLVED on the alpha ladder ({ui-a:…}): {black-a.7} in light, {white-a.8} in dark for the default system.
Color Semantics.Border/focus: [ROLE: A11y Focus Ring] Affects the keyboard focus-visible ring on every interactive element. SOLVED per theme ({ui:accent.9}), not pinned — the ring is always the user's own accent hue, so a fixed tone cannot promise a floor. Walks the accent ramp from tone 9 until WCAG 1.4.11 + APCA Lc 45 both clear: light lands on 9-11 depending on hue, dark on 11 for the seeds tested. Deliberate scope: this is the ONLY focus ring, incl. on an invalid/critical field — focus wins over the error colour rather than a separate border.focus.critical, keeping one ring token instead of one per severity. That covers the solid BOUNDARY only — the translucent halo is border.ring.*.
Color Semantics.Border/ring/default: [ROLE: Focus Halo] Translucent glow outside border.focus. Paired with border.focus on EVERY focused control (shadcn border-ring + ring-[3px]): the edge turns to border.focus, this halo sits outside it. Never the only focus cue. Decoration, NOT a boundary — never measured for WCAG 1.4.11; border.focus is the contrast-bearing part. Replaces a hardcoded 40% alpha in the preview specimens. A field in an error/success state reuses status.<sev>.border for its halo — there is no separate per-severity ring role.
Color Semantics.Border/rim-highlight: [ROLE: Elevation Rim] 1px light rim along the top of an elevated surface in dark mode. Below a near-black page only ~5% of the luminance range is left to spend downward, so elevation has to be bought with light, not shadow — this is the token for the rim darkShadow() already paints.
Color Semantics.Border/accent: [ROLE: Accent Border] Border painted in the brand accent — a selected card, a toggled button, any element that needs its stroke to read as the primary accent. For keyboard focus use border.focus.

Radius.role/control: Checkbox, nested child, menu item, inner thumb.

Spacing.role/gap-tight: Icon + label, chip dismiss, inline meta.
Spacing.role/gap-control: Button groups, OTP cells, field + helper.
Spacing.role/inset-page: Page and sheet margins when Grid is unused.
Spacing.role/overlap-xl: Heavily stacked; only the edge shows.
Spacing.role/overlap-2xl: Nearly fully covered — a count badge on a stack.

Size.role/hit: Close button and icon-only hit area.

Selector.role/compact: The same glyphs in a dense row or table.
Selector.role/indicator: Badge dot, status pip, unread marker.

Border.role/focus: Focus-ring width: the inner edge of a focused control (the halo adds one more hairline). Paint stays border.focus.

Grid.role/mobile: Max-width of the 4-col grid (one step below Tablet).
Grid.columns: Tracks in the layout grid. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Grid.gutter: Gap between columns — a spacing step. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Grid.margin: Page inset below the container cap — a spacing step. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Grid.container: Max content width — a breakpoint step, or none. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.

Typography.role/display/size: Hero and page titles. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/heading-xl/size: Largest section title. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/heading-lg/size: Primary section heading. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/heading-md/size: Card and panel titles. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/heading-sm/size: Nested headings and list titles. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/heading-xs/size: Overline-scale titles still read as headings. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/heading-xs/weight: Overline-scale titles still read as headings.
Typography.role/heading-xs/family: Overline-scale titles still read as headings.
Typography.role/heading-2xs/size: Smallest heading (h6). Sits one rung above body. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/heading-2xs/weight: Smallest heading (h6). Sits one rung above body.
Typography.role/heading-2xs/family: Smallest heading (h6). Sits one rung above body.
Typography.role/body-lg/size: Lead paragraphs. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/body-md/size: Default reading size. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/body-sm/size: Dense supporting copy. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/label/size: Form labels and field names. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/placeholder/size: Input placeholder and empty-field hint. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/caption/size: Image captions and metadata. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/button/size: Control labels — buttons, tabs, chips. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
Typography.role/helper/size: Field help, validation, footnotes. One value per viewport mode: Desktop · Tablet · Mobile.
